answer: Each agent must lock a scarce deposit before it can submit work, and the protocol slashes that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud. A single operator can still create a fable of many identities, but every one must tie up real capital; splitting the stake does not multiply voting weight. In a falcon-like audit, randomly sampled tasks are checked against signed outputs, so fake agents risk losing deposits as well as the cost of keeping them locked. The oasis is trust earned through verified work, not a cheap new name.
